questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's MCP guide say a malicious server can do?

options.text: Only slow down responses; it can't touch any data.
options.explanation: The guide warns about much more: data exfiltration and hidden instructions.

options.text: Exfiltrate sensitive data from anything that enters the model's context.
options.explanation: Right. That is why the guide says to trust any remote server you use.

options.text: Change the AI model's training data for all customers.
options.explanation: The guide's warnings are about your requests and data, not the model's training.

questions.prompt: Under Anthropic's managed MCP settings, a server matches both the allowlist and the denylist. What happens?

options.text: It is allowed, because the allowlist is checked first.
options.explanation: The page's example says the opposite.

options.text: The user is asked to choose each time.
options.explanation: The page gives a fixed rule, not a user choice.

options.text: It is blocked, because the denylist takes precedence.
options.explanation: Right. The managed MCP page's example says the denylist takes precedence.

questions.prompt: Anthropic's MCP connector page recommends one approach for read-only assistants. Which one?

options.text: Denylist the write or destructive tools.
options.explanation: Right. The page recommends this for read-only assistants, or when you want a human to confirm changes.

options.text: Turn on every tool and trust the model's judgement.
options.explanation: The page offers allowlists and denylists so you don't have to rely on that.

options.text: Use a different MCP server for each user.
options.explanation: The page's recommendation is about which tools are on, not one server per user.
